entry.title: Physical AI System Design for Warehousing and Intralogistics: What the Published Designs Already Answer
entry.summary: No warehousing design has been published in this series yet. Nine of the eighteen open reference architectures already answer the questions a warehouse or distribution center asks first: one picture of the operation from the systems it already runs, dock and yard turn time, people and vehicles seen on camera, fleet and fixed equipment condition, fire and life safety, counting what leaves, and what a records only study can settle before any sensor is bought.

entry.title: Physical AI System Design for Mining: What the Published Designs Already Answer
entry.summary: No mining design has been published in this series yet. Eight of the eighteen open reference architectures already answer the questions a mine asks first: people and vehicles on haul roads, mobile fleet and fixed plant condition, incidents before they happen, fire and life safety, counting what leaves the plant, and what a records-only study can settle before any sensor is bought.

entry.title: From a CISA Advisory to a Closed Finding
entry.summary: What an operational technology security team does with an advisory about an actively exploited vulnerability, traced through one published system of context: the advisory becomes a threat intelligence item, the item seeds detection rules, a finding scores the operator's own assets, a named analyst accepts or rejects the risk, and the evidence a NERC CIP audit asks for is assembled on the way.

entry.title: The Model Register Across Sixteen Designs
entry.summary: Sixteen open reference architectures for physical operations, each with a model register the operator owns outright. Twelve models, four empty registers by decision, and one licence pattern that repeats in every design.

entry.title: Sensing Comes Before the Model
entry.summary: Three published earth observation architectures decide what to watch from law, revisit and ownership, never from model accuracy. Two of the three ship with an empty model register.

entry.title: Own or Rent the GPUs
entry.summary: Seven published reference architectures, priced the same way, say owning the reasoning node costs between about half and nearly all of the deepest three year cloud commitment. Not a tenth.

entry.title: Don't Baptize the GPUs
entry.summary: Why AI systems should be measured by running them, trained to seek truth and owned by the organizations that depend on them, rather than blessed into a theological category.
